arrival_point_rule.ruling: COO-DECISION 20260829_0542 (pf_bridge/notes_to_chief/20260829_0542_COO-DECISION-marker-table-is-the-default-spawn-source-with-an-evidence-label.md), answering LANE-A's 20260829_0447 ask. Accepted as a STANDING rule of the project, so a scene with a marker no longer needs a per-scene decision to get an arrival point.
arrival_point_rule.rule_1_default_source: A scene whose SCENE_NAME[n].n_MARKER != 0 takes MARKER[n_MARKER] as its arrival point, with no per-scene ruling asked for. A scene whose n_MARKER == 0 keeps every older rule unchanged - client evidence, an owner decree, or refusal - and inventing a coordinate remains forbidden. 13 of the client's 271 scenes carry a non-zero n_MARKER.
arrival_point_rule.rule_2_indirect_read_only: MANDATORY INDIRECTION, AND IT IS A PROHIBITION RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE: resolve through SCENE_NAME[n].n_MARKER, never by indexing MARKER with a scene id. Measured reason, and it is why the prohibition is needed rather than obvious - the shortcut AGREES with the crosswalk on 12 of the 13 marker scenes, so it will look correct to whoever introduces it: it hands scene 130 another map's row (scene 130 names marker 1000), and 19-12=7 MARKER rows carry n_ID == n_SCENE while not being the row their own scene named, so for seven scene ids the shortcut returns a row that passes a naive back-pointer check and is still not that scene's arrival point. The count 7 is exact (each of the 12 necessarily has n_ID == n_SCENE, since its row names its scene back); what those seven ARE is deliberately not claimed - scene 130 names marker 1000, so a MARKER[130] row carrying n_SCENE 130 would be one of the seven and would belong to a scene that has a marker rather than to one with none. Settling that needs the full 390-row table, which is in the bridge repo. src/pirateforce_foundation/world_scene_marker.py:forbidden_direct_index_scenes() is this rule as arithmetic.
arrival_point_rule.rule_3_evidence_tier: A marker-sourced point is evidence tier 'authored' - the map's developers wrote that coordinate down - UNLESS an attended or runtime pass has actually stood a client on that exact point, which is the only thing that raises it. Scene 2 is the one row in this file that has cleared that bar (MARKER[2] was the coordinate, and SCENE-001 then loaded and rendered Prison Exile Island with a client standing on it, docs/EXPERIMENT_LEDGER.md:32), so it reads 'client-observed' while still being from_marker true. Every other marker-sourced row is 'authored' and MUST NOT be promoted to confirmed until an attended round stands a client on it and a human looks (COO-DECISION 20260828_2250 still governs promotion, unchanged by this ruling). CORRECTED after pf-adversary (round 8ubiku, D6): the first version of this sentence read 'It is NOT client-observed' flatly, which was false of scene 2 one hundred lines below it in this same file, and the test that was supposed to enforce the ceiling hard-coded scene 2 out of its own loop rather than the rule stating its exception. Every row carries coordinate_provenance naming the marker it came from, or saying explicitly that it came from something else, plus deviates_from_rule_1 for the one case (scene 1) that has a marker and declines it. ENFORCEMENT, because the first version of this rule was a self-report: world_scene_travel's loader now decides whether rule 1 reaches a scene from table_row.n_MARKER - the client's own column - not from the row's from_marker flag, and a row claiming a marker must name the marker its table row names AND stand on that marker's pinned coordinate. A row can no longer vote itself out of the rule, which is exactly what it could do before (pf-adversary D2/D3).
arrival_point_rule.what_this_ruling_did_not_do: It did not open any door. Scene 14's login_entry_allowed stays false (set by LANE-A round vyi2ud after pf-adversary measured three defects, re-confirmed by chief letter 20260829_0520). Giving a scene an address is not wiring a scene. The COO also ordered that the rule may not be applied to a sixth scene until this text is on main, so the rule and its first use cannot land in one unreviewed step.
arrival_point_rule.how_this_rule_falls: GT-134 is its first proof. The COO's own words: if the tester surfaces in rock, in lava, or under the floor, this rule falls immediately and LANE-A reverts under item 4 of its own 0447 letter without asking again.
arrival_point_rule.carve_out_scene_1_home_is_not_retro_move: [LANE-A ASSUMPTION - AWAITING COO CONFIRMATION] Scene 1 HAS n_MARKER = 1, so rule 1 read literally would replace the spawn this runtime has stood every new character on since V135 with MARKER[1] - a point 2340.22 units away in XY and 2382.66 in three dimensions. LANE-A reads rule 1 as a DEFAULT FOR A SCENE THAT DOES NOT ALREADY HAVE AN ARRIVAL POINT IN USE, not as a retro-correction of one that does, because the COO's own reasoning calls the rule 'a default, not a truth' and states in the same letter that MARKER[1] being 2200-odd units from the live spawn is why. ground.limit: a .npc file carries NPC placements, not terrain. Flat placement z is evidence about where the developer put mobs, NOT a measurement of the ground mesh, and it says nothing about walls, water, sky or lighting. The eye check in the attended ticket is what decides whether this is the white flat stage the owner asked for.

scene 14 is pinned with login_entry_allowed FALSE, and the three measured reasons are the whole of why. Round vyi2ud first pinned it TRUE - a character could then log into Hell Volcano Island through the per-account login-scene override, and pf-adversary drove that login end to end before it left draft. (1) THE WRONG CENSUS SHIPS: runtime.py's census dispatch reads foundation.selected.position.scene_id, the STORED row, which the override never rewrites - it still says 1 - so the guard at runtime.py:6114 ('away from home the bg0001 census is not merely useless, it is wrong') never fires and 108 Port Royal dock NPCs, every one encoded scene_id=1, are sent anchored on the volcano. (2) THE CHARACTER ROW IS CORRUPTED, SILENTLY: _checkpoint_exact_target builds its candidate from the same stored scene id, so is_position_persist_allowed is asked about scene 1 (answer: yes) and never about scene 14 - a walk on the island writes (scene_id 1, volcano XYZ) into character_positions, which is byte-for-byte the GT-106 incident persist_position_allowed was created to prevent, and the next login prints no relocation line because scene 1 takes the home branch. persist_position_allowed=false for scene 14 is therefore DEAD CONFIG on the only path that reaches the scene. (3) THE FACTION BYTE IS DROPPED: the faction-1 compose refuses for any scene but 2 and Port Royal (runtime.py:5532), so a scene-14 login emits no PLAYER_FACTION line at all - and HYP-PF-027 proved hostility renders from the faction pair, on the one ticket whose question is whether living things appear.

THE QUESTION THAT HAS TO BE ANSWERED BEFORE ANY per-scene KEY IN THIS FILE MEANS ANYTHING (pf-adversary, round vyi2ud, closing finding): when a character's stored row and the scene the client is standing in disagree, which one is the character in? Every guard this project has built - the census branch, is_position_persist_allowed, the faction recompose, _checkpoint_exact_target, the GM warp confirm token - reads the STORED row. resolve_entry returns a different answer in entry.position and the override path deliberately never writes it back. Until one of the two is named the authority, login_entry_allowed and persist_position_allowed are keys on a door the runtime walks past. This is not scene 14's problem: the same three defects reproduce today, on main, for an override into scene 2 or scene 278, both of which are pinned here with login entry allowed by default.

scene 14 ground is null ON PURPOSE, and the number that decides it is measured: Bg0015's 91 placements span 40312.777 x 46416.541 units, so a ground block derived from them the way scenes 1 and 278 derive theirs would be a box wide enough to swallow almost any stored row. pf-adversary built exactly that block and drove it: a Port Royal row sits 8273 x 21819 units from marker 14, inside the box, and resolve_entry KEEPS it - the character stands at Port Royal's coordinates inside the volcano. CORRECTION to this round's first wording, which said that happens 'silently': it does not. _kept_row_line prints WORLD_SCENE_KEPT_ROW with both coordinates. The decision stands on the keep, not on silence, and the silence claim was withdrawn before this file left draft (pf-adversary D8). A later round that measures real terrain may add ground; a later round that adds the placement bounding box as ground is undoing this on purpose and should read this line first.

scene 14 persist_position_allowed is false, and its justification has been REWRITTEN after pf-adversary refuted the original. It was written as a safety property - 'the tester's Port Royal row is never touched, so removing the override puts them back exactly where they were'. Measured, that sentence is false: on the override path the gate is never asked about scene 14 at all (see the login_entry_allowed nonclaim above), and the row IS overwritten with volcano coordinates under scene id 1. The key is kept at false because it is the correct value the day the runtime asks about the scene a character is actually in - not because it protects anything today. The client's own row says n_SAVE 1, so the value to expect after that fix is true.
